description: Raven is Ouranos's open-source server for hydrological data preparation and catchment analysis. It exposes data collection, geoprocessing and watershed delineation through the Web Processing Service standard. Inputs can include digital elevation models and land-use layers; outputs include delineated catchments and derived watershed properties. Geographic coverage and grid resolution depend on the source layers; there is no fixed observation period for the software. The MIT-licensed server can be installed locally or through Docker, and a hosted PAVICS endpoint is described. A limitation is that operation depends on external geospatial datasets and WPS deployment; the README points to a separate Python client for convenient access. It prepares features for hydrological or water-infrastructure modelling but is not itself a rainfall-runoff simulator. This Raven is distinct from other models with the same name. The server and docs were inspected without calling the hosted service or obtaining data. It complements hydrological simulators by preparing catchment geometries and attributes.
